Rodin::Math module

Spatial arithmetic, matrix operations, and sparse linear algebra.

SpatialVector and SpatialMatrix support small spatial calculations without heap allocation. Vector, Matrix, and their fixed-size counterparts provide Eigen-compatible algebra; LinearSystem groups system data and constraint elimination. These types support geometric mappings, constitutive calculations, assembly, and linear solves.

Usage

Include <Rodin/Math.h> and <utility> for these examples. The names below assume using namespace Rodin; and using namespace Rodin::Math;.

Spatial arithmetic

Small spatial vectors support scalar products, cross products, and norms.

SpatialVector<Real> a{1, 2, 3};
SpatialVector<Real> b{4, 5, 6};
const Real product = dot(a, b);       // 32
const auto normal = a.cross(b);      // {-3, 6, -3}
const Real length = a.norm();        // sqrt(14)

Dense and fixed-size algebra

Dynamic and fixed-size types support Eigen-compatible initialization and expressions. Store an expression in a concrete type to retain its result.

Matrix<Real> A(2, 2);
A << 2, -1,
    -1,  2;
Vector<Real> x(2);
x << 1, 2;
Vector<Real> y = A * x;              // {0, 3}

FixedSizeMatrix<Real, 2, 2> fixedA = A;
FixedSizeVector<Real, 2> fixedX = x;
FixedSizeVector<Real, 2> fixedY = fixedA * fixedX;

Sparse matrices

Insert entries and compress the matrix before using its CSC storage.

SparseMatrix<Real> A(3, 3);
A.insert(0, 0) = 2;
A.insert(1, 1) = 3;
A.insert(2, 2) = 4;
A.makeCompressed();

Vector<Real> x = Vector<Real>::Ones(3);
Vector<Real> y = A * x;              // {2, 3, 4}

Complex scalar products

The scalar product conjugates its right-hand operand:

SpatialVector<Complex> a{Complex(1, 1), Complex(2, 0)};
SpatialVector<Complex> b{Complex(0, 1), Complex(3, 0)};
const Complex product = dot(a, b);   // 7 - i

Angles and constants

Convert degrees to radians explicitly; mathematical functions accept the underlying scalar value.

const Rad angle = Deg(180).toRad();
const Real radians = Real(angle);    // pi
const Real halfTurn = Constants::pi();
const Real sine = sin(radians);      // approximately zero

Time integration

Advance by one time step with the classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. Supply the current state separately from the output.

const Real current = 1;
Real next = 0;
RungeKutta::RK4 integrator;
integrator.step(next, 0.1, current, [](Real q) { return -q; });
// next approximates exp(-0.1).

Scalar root finding

Find by solving in a bracket. The callable returns the function value and derivative; the result is an Optional containing the root when the iteration succeeds.

RootFinding::NewtonRaphson<Real> solver;
const auto root = solver.solve(
  [](Real x) { return std::make_pair(x * x - 2, 2 * x); },
  1.5, 1.0, 2.0);

template<class ScalarType>
using SparseMatrix = Eigen::SparseMatrix<ScalarType, Eigen::ColMajor, SparseIndex>

Defined in Rodin/Math/SparseMatrix.h

Sparse matrix type.

Template parameters
ScalarType The element type (e.g., Real, Complex)

A sparse matrix stores only the non-zero elements, making it memory-efficient for large matrices arising from finite element discretizations where most entries are zero. The matrix uses compressed column storage (CCS) format by default.

Storage Format

Eigen's SparseMatrix uses Compressed Column Storage (CCS), also known as Compressed Sparse Column (CSC) format, which stores:

  • Non-zero values
  • Signed 32-bit row indices for each non-zero value
  • Signed 32-bit column pointers indicating where each column starts

Typical Applications

  • Stiffness matrices: in
  • Mass matrices: in
  • Discretized differential operators

template<class LHSScalar, class RHSScalar>
auto dot(const SpatialVector<LHSScalar>& lhs, const SpatialVector<RHSScalar>& rhs) constexpr

Defined in Rodin/Math/Common.h

Computes the dot product of two SpatialVector objects.

Template parameters
LHSScalar Scalar type of left-hand side
RHSScalar Scalar type of right-hand side
Parameters
lhs in Left-hand side SpatialVector
rhs in Right-hand side SpatialVector
Returns Dot product (scalar)

For logical dimension , computes . Real operands use scalar contractions; complex operands retain fixed-extent reductions with right conjugation. Mixed scalar products retain their dynamic reduction. Fused arithmetic and reduction order may differ within floating-point rounding. Inactive storage is never read; the empty product is zero.

Computes over active entries. Real matrices retain dimension-specific kernels in one shape dispatch, shared with the member dot operation. Full-size storage uses Eigen's fixed reduction directly; smaller shapes use explicit active entries. Empty shapes return zero without reading inactive storage.
